listing.name: Colin McRae Rally 2.0 / OpenCMR2
listing.summary: Explore Colin McRae Rally 2.0 / OpenCMR2 and follow the upstream project for requirements, downloads and setup.

steps.title: Supply your original game files on first launch
steps.instruction: Select your installed original Colin McRae Rally 2.0 game folder when OpenCMR2 asks on first launch. The supported original files can stay outside the managed runtime. An optional Data folder beside the executable is carried between compatible versions.

steps.title: Keep your progress and choose when to update
steps.instruction: OpenCMR2 normally keeps saves, settings and logs in AppData/OpenCMR2, outside Portcove backups. Declared Data and in-folder fallback opencmr2.ini/opencmr2.log are retained when present. The upstream game owns edition checks and its storage resolver; Portcove replaces the package only. Portcove uses the selected channel and update policy. Runtime rollback carries declared current data; it does not rewind saves or guarantee older-game compatibility. Linux normally uses ~/.local/share/OpenCMR2. Keep the packaged libSDL3.so.0 beside opencmr2; the game needs that companion library.

presentation.manual_preparation: Select your installed original Colin McRae Rally 2.0 game folder when OpenCMR2 asks on first launch. The supported original files can stay outside the managed runtime. An optional Data folder beside the executable is carried between compatible versions. OpenCMR2 normally keeps saves, settings and logs in AppData/OpenCMR2, outside Portcove backups. Declared Data and in-folder fallback opencmr2.ini/opencmr2.log are retained when present. The upstream game owns edition checks and its storage resolver; Portcove replaces the package only. Existing external installations keep their files and update ownership. Play has not been tested through Portcove. The declared SaveGame folder also preserves the upstream user-directory fallback. If preference storage fails or custom launch paths create other files in the runtime, keep the current copy and review those exact paths before replacement; use external registration for custom storage. Linux normally uses ~/.local/share/OpenCMR2. Keep the packaged libSDL3.so.0 beside opencmr2; the game needs that companion library. Play has not been tested through Portcove on Linux.
